_README: Named SUBJECTS a headless lane can be pointed at, consumed by ops/loop/scope.py.
Point a lane at one for a single run with CLOCKSPEED_LANE_SCOPE_<LANE>=<name>;
for the queue lane that is CLOCKSPEED_LANE_SCOPE_QUEUE=dashboard.
THE LANE NAME IS UPPER-CASED AND ITS HYPHEN KEPT, so queue-b reads
CLOCKSPEED_LANE_SCOPE_QUEUE-B. PowerShell sets that only in the braced form,
${env:CLOCKSPEED_LANE_SCOPE_QUEUE-B} = '<name>' - the bare $env: form does not
parse - and a POSIX shell cannot export it; env(1) can pass it to one child. Set
it in the shell that runs ops/loop/launch_queue_loop.ps1, for that process only,
never at user or machine scope: the driver and every worker inherit it from there.
A SCOPE THAT NAMES AN anchor_phase IS A PARTITION, NOT A LIST, AND THAT IS WHAT
STOPS IT SHRINKING IN SILENCE. Every takeable row of the anchor phase must be
either in items or in excluded with a written reason. Delete an id from items
and it becomes UNCLASSIFIED: the lane REFUSES naming it, and the arm
tests/ops/test_lane_scope.py::test_the_dashboard_scope_partitions_its_anchor_phase
goes RED. A first cut of this file was a bare list whose length nothing graded -
cutting it from eight ids to two left the whole suite green while the lane served
a quarter of its queue. That is why excluded exists and why it carries reasons.
items MAY name rows outside the anchor phase - CS-962 is one - and those are
additions the partition does not account for, so they are pinned by a second
enumeration in the test module instead.
MAINTENANCE. When a member closes, delete its id from items. When a NEW row is
filed under the anchor phase, put it in items or in excluded with a reason; until
then the lane refuses and names it. Never delete an id from items and add it to
excluded to quiet a red without saying why - the reason field is the whole point.
Do not add a phase gate row and do not add a docs/GATED.md id; both are refused
anyway - tools/headless-queue.md section 5 FENCE 1 and FENCE 2.

save-reader.description: The CS-1038 block: the save reader's container-element and world-seam decode gaps, filed together by one review and worked as one unit. AN ENUMERATION, NOT A PARTITION, AND DELIBERATELY SO - '## Phase 4 - save reader' carries 140 takeable rows, so anchoring here would need 138 exclusion entries with written reasons, and an exclusion reason invented to quiet a red is the exact abuse the dashboard scope's reason field exists to prevent. A short named block is graded per member instead: every id here is checked against the live ROADMAP.md for closure, gating, gate-row shape and absence by test_the_declared_scopes_all_validate_against_the_live_roadmap, which iterates every declared scope. CS-1038 and CS-1040 are members of the same review block and are NOT here because both CLOSED on 2026-09-13; a closed row is never takeable, so neither is ever re-added.

dashboard.description: The dashboard surface subject. NOT expressible as a phase filter: it partitions '## Phase 6 - surfaces' and additionally pulls in CS-962, the row that says the dashboard renders nothing a player would act on, which sits in the phase 4 block entirely.

advisor-ranking.description: A PRODUCT subject for the queue lane, filed in session 150 under CLAUDE.md section 7's product-before-process rule: how cards and plans are ordered, and the stores and optimizer that ordering reads. WRITE AREA, judged from each row's acceptance and the code it names: clockspeed/advisor/advise.py and cards.py (CS-1246's quick-win order, CS-1247's domain interleave), clockspeed/advisor/ledger.py (CS-1246's aging count, CS-1253's versioned stores), and clockspeed/solve/optimize.py with clockspeed/solve/backends/ (CS-1245's bounded enumeration). CS-1244 CLOSED 2026-10-22 and is gone from items; its credit to cards.py is CORRECTED here rather than merely dropped, because it was measured WRONG ON THE CODE. The badge's home is clockspeed/solve/strategy.py, a consumer sibling above the optimizer interface, and never the card: Card is frozen with exactly one field, trace, and advise() is built from audit models and unlock state with no plan reaching it, so a badge field on the card would have had no producer - cards.py and advise.py were UNCHANGED by that close. The remaining gap is the ROADMAP row CS-1346, and CS-1347 beside it; neither is a member of any scope yet, and this file is the wrong place to make one. CS-1253 IS HERE, NOT WITH THE SAVE ROWS, because CS-1246 ages a card by an evaluation count the ledger does not store, so both rows edit ledger.py and one lane serialises them. AN ENUMERATION, NOT A PARTITION: anchoring '## Phase 5' would need every other lane's rows as exclusions. Graded per member by test_the_declared_scopes_all_validate_against_the_live_roadmap.

registry-audit.description: A PRODUCT subject for the queue-b lane, filed in session 150: registry integrity and audit totals. WRITE AREA: clockspeed/data/registry.py, docs_extract.py and version.py (CS-1241's build-aware variants and decisions table, CS-1242's extraction census against the pinned build) and clockspeed/audit/ (CS-1250's count-once invariant). CS-1250 IS HERE because CS-1242's docs-versus-save agreement can only sit where the registry and the world model meet, which is clockspeed/audit/, and both rows would then edit that package's export list. CS-1240 IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: it re-keys every registry and save join, which spans data/, audit/, surface/ and the progress/ schematic join CS-1343 is building, and CS-1343's clause forbids a name-matching heuristic beside that join while CS-1240 adds one normalised fallback. An adjudicator rules whether the fallback reaches that join before CS-1240 joins any scope. AN ENUMERATION, NOT A PARTITION, graded per member.
